title.narrative: Inclusive transformation for youth and child-friendly local governance in Uzbekistan-01003551

description.narrative: The Joint Programme Inclusive Transformation for Youth and Child-Friendly Local Governance in Uzbekistan aims to strengthen the inclusiveness, transparency, and responsiveness of local governance systems by empowering local authorities to strategically plan, budget, and deliver services in line with the needs of vulnerable groups, particularly children, youth, women, the elderly, and people with disabilities. Through a results-based management (RBM) and results-based budgeting (RBB) approach,

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

title.narrative: Number of local government action plans developed using RBM and RBB principles to address the needs of children, youth, and vulnerable groups.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of Action Plans prepared by local governance bodies (khokimiyats, kengashes, and makhallas) that explicitly apply Results-Based Management (RBM) and Results-Based Budgeting (RBB) principles. Action Plans must be developed through participatory approaches, align strategic goals with measurable targets and indicators, and link budgets to outcomes addressing the specific needs of children, adolescents, youth, and vulnerable groups.

title.narrative: Number of pilot districts that develop and implement local coordination and cooperation models supporting services for children, adolescents, youth, and their families

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of pilot districts that define, adopt, and implement new or improved coordination models to strengthen local cooperation among service providers (e.g., education, health, social services, mahallas) for the benefit of children, adolescents, youth, and their families. A functional model must demonstrate clear roles and responsibilities among local actors, mechanisms for cross-sectoral collaboration, and improved service responsiveness to community needs.

title.narrative: Percentage of regional and local development strategies that incorporate Results-Based Management (RBM) and Results-Based Budgeting (RBB) principles

description.narrative: This indicator measures the proportion of regional and local development strategies that explicitly integrate RBM and RBB principles into their planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation frameworks. RBM and RBB principles include the formulation of clear results chains (outcomes, outputs, activities), establishment of measurable performance indicators, setting of outcome/output targets, and alignment of budget allocations with strategic objectives.

title.narrative: Number of adolescent boys and girls, young women and men participated in the consultations with the LG

description.narrative: This indicator captures the number of adolescents and youth (boys and girls, young women and men) who actively participated in structured consultations with local governments. It includes participation through platforms such as Youth Advisory Boards, Youth and Khokim dialogues, and digital platforms like U-Report. The indicator reflects efforts to institutionalize youth participation in decision-making processes at the local level.

title.narrative: Number of adolescent girls and boys who participated in or led offline and online civic engagement initiatives in their communities

description.narrative: This indicator measures the number of functional youth engagement platforms — such as Youth Advisory Boards, participatory budgeting platforms, U-Report digital platforms, or other formal mechanisms — established or strengthened at the local level to enable meaningful participation of adolescents and youth in local governance, service delivery monitoring, and decision-making processes. Platforms must be operational, inclusive, and allow youth to voice their needs, priorities, and proposals.

title.narrative: Improvement in the capacity of local government officials to utilize RBM and RBB principles

description.narrative: This indicator measures the extent to which the capacity of local government officials (khokimiyats, kengashes, and makhallas) has been strengthened to apply Results-Based Management (RBM) and Results-Based Budgeting (RBB) principles in their planning, budgeting, and public administration processes. It assesses the progress from baseline capacity (pre-training assessment) to improved competency levels (post-training assessment) after capacity-building interventions under the Joint Programme. Baseline (2023): Average score of 30% in pre-training assessments. Target: 40% average score in post-training assessments by 2025; 80% average score in post-training assessments by 2028. Means of Verification: Training assessment reports; Participant feedback surveys; Independent performance evaluations; Certification program completion records. Rationale: Strengthening the technical and institutional capacities of local government officials is critical to institutionalizing RBM and RBB practices, ensuring better strategic planning, resource management, accountability, and service delivery. It supports the broader goal of establishing coherent, inclusive, and results-driven local governance systems in Uzbekistan. Key Activities Contributing to the Indicator: Conducting institutional analysis, functional review, and business process reengineering of local governance bodies; Developing and delivering customized RBM and RBB training and certification programs; Supporting the application of RBM and RBB in developing local development strategies and budget programs; Monitoring and evaluating officials' competencies through standardized pre- and post-training assessments. Key Assumptions: Sufficient political commitment and allocation of human and financial resources for capacity development. Active participation and engagement of local officials in the training and certification programs. Risk Factors: Potential turnover of trained local government staff. Insufficient follow-up support or institutional resistance to adopting RBM/RBB principles.

title.narrative: Percentage of (vulnerable) population satisfied with public and social services delivery by supported state authorities according to key human rights criteria and principles.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the percentage of women, youth, children, the elderly, and people with disabilities in pilot regions who report satisfaction with the quality, adequacy, and responsiveness of local public and social services. It reflects improvements in evidence-based planning, results-based budgeting, and coordination among local governance bodies as a result of the project’s capacity-building efforts.
